subject: Decanting acceptance windows & surge containment — proposed MAP amendment
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthsync.com>, Julia Morales <julia@healthsync.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-10T16:12:00Z
Subject: Decanting acceptance windows & surge containment — proposed MAP amendment

Hi Samir / Julia,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on your update on procurement timing, I sketch a small change to the mutual action plan (attached) to reduce risk to your go‑live while preserving the acceptance gates you need. High level:

- Split Acceptance into Phase A (core API + small sample workload) and Phase B (full volume) to decant the acceptance windows.
- Proposed Phase A target: 2 weeks after pilot sign-off; Phase B: up to 4 weeks after Phase A start.
- Temporary surge containment: Redwood will reserve burst capacity for a 72hr ramp during Phase B start.
- Financial concession: 10% credit applied to the first invoice if Phase B starts >30 days past original MAP date (we can discuss).

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (annotated).

Can you confirm whether procurement needs a DocuSign amendment, or if a formal PO and this MAP note will suffice? Low friction is the goal here.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm procurement constraints (timeline + approver).
2) We circulate an amendment draft for legal/procurement review (I can own).
3) Exec intro if needed.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0136
From: Samir Patel <samir@healthsync.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Julia Morales <julia@healthsync.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: 2026-06-11T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Decanting acceptance windows & surge containment — proposed MAP amendment

Hi Rachel —

Appreciate the proactive proposal. Procurement flagged a queue backlog; realistic earliest sign-off for Phase B is the week of July 5. Phase A sounds workable — we want to avoid blocking the pilot.

A couple quick asks from our side:
- Can you outline the exact operational cutover activities for Phase A so our SREs can scope the pilot?
- Procurement asked whether the 10% credit is contractual or goodwill — they need something that maps to the PO.

I copied procurement (procurement@healthsync.com). I can also loop in our CTO if you want an exec-to-exec alignment — maybe after we lock Phase A details.

Best,
Samir
Head of Partnerships | HealthSync
samir@healthsync.com

Rachel / Camila —

Saw Samir's note. Two short options we should prepare for the thread with procurement:

Option 1 — Decant/Phase approach (recommended):
- Phase A: pilot acceptance (smaller dataset) — sign-off by HealthSync SREs.
- Phase B: full volume acceptance — start window moved to week of 2026-07-05.
- Redwood provides 72hr burst and 10% invoice credit tied to an amendment (DocuSign).

Option 2 — No amendment, credit as a one-time invoice note:
- Faster to finalize but procurement may push back without contractual leverage.

I also suggest we prep a short operational checklist for Phase A (cutover steps, monitoring playbook, rollback criteria) that Rachel can send to their SREs. Camila — can you draft the checklist and the short amendment with scope/credit language?

If procurement insists on a PO-only approach we pivot to Option 2 and raise the exec flag. Jonas — do you want to handle the exec intro if we need it?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Sr. Account Manager | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, rachel.kim@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-13T11:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Decanting acceptance windows & surge containment — exec path and amendment

All —

I can take the exec intro if it becomes necessary. Draft plan from my side:

- We propose a two-stage amendment (attached draft): Phase A acceptance criteria + Phase B start window with an explicit credit clause.
- Request DocuSign for the amendment so procurement has a clear contractual artifact. Link to placeholder DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/placeholder-amendment
- Camila, please attach the Phase A operational checklist to the amendment.
- Rachel, include the SRE contact and proposed pilot dates; we should aim for a short pilot (7–10 days) that proves stability.

If procurement still resists, we offer a temporary SLA delta for Phase B (reduced throughput guarantees with a price protection credit) until full volume is accepted.

Attachment: Amendment_draft.docx

Jonas Weber
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@healthsync.com>, procurement@healthsync.com
Cc: camila.reyes@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T18:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Decanting acceptance windows & surge containment — amendment & next steps

Samir / Procurement team —

Thanks for the context. Per our internal review (Ben / Camila / Jonas looped), we are proposing the following formalized path:

1) MAP amendment (attached) that decants Acceptance into Phase A and Phase B. Phase A is a 7–10 day pilot focused on core API traffic; Phase B is full volume acceptance targeted for the week of July 5.
2) Financial concession: 10% credit on the first invoice if Phase B start date is >30 days past the original MAP Acceptance date. This will be captured in the DocuSign amendment so procurement has contractual clarity.
3) Operational checklist for Phase A is attached (see MAP_v2.xlsx). Camila will send a separate checklist doc to your SREs with cutover steps and rollback criteria.

Action items:
- procurement@healthsync.com: Please confirm whether DocuSign is acceptable and provide the approver name/PO cadence.
- Samir: confirm proposed pilot start windows (we recommended June 22 or June 29).
- Rachel (me): I'll circulate the DocuSign amendment once procurement confirms approver details.

If procurement needs immediate exec engagement, Jonas will set a short call. Otherwise we should be able to close this amendment without delaying the overall timeline substantially.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, Amendment_draft.docx

Best,
Rachel Kim
